Lessons.Title: Transformation of Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals: shift graphs vertically and horizontally, reflect about axes, identify even/odd symmetry, stretch/compress inputs and outputs, and combine several transformations while tracking original domain restrictions.
For g(x)=f(x)+k output values shift up or down by k. For g(x)=f(x−h), graph moves right h despite the subtraction inside.

For −f(x), negate the output, reflecting across horizontal x-axis. For f(−x), negate each input to reflect across the vertical y-axis. An even function is unchanged under f(−x); an odd function changes to −f(x).
Multiplying outputs g(x)=a f(x) gives vertical scaling; multiplying inputs g(x)=f(bx) changes horizontal scaling inversely. Negative factors may add reflection.
A contextual formula's units reveal whether the change is to an input or to an output. Never add miles directly to dollars or years directly to population.
For combined transformations apply the input substitution and output scaling carefully, then check vertex/endpoints, asymptotes and domain.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: (a) For f(x)=|x| give the vertex and range of g(x)=2f(x−3)−4. (b) For h(x)=√x explain the domain of h(−x). (c) Determine if p(x)=x³−5x is odd, even, or neither.
Independent Try It 1 — Model vertical shift. A ball's height is h(t)=−5t²+30t metres. Write new height b(t) if launched 8 m above ground.
Independent Try It 2 — Root horizontal shift. For f(x)=√x, graph g(x)=f(x+2). Give new startpoint and domain.
Independent Try It 3 — Absolute-value translation. For f(x)=|x|, graph h(x)=f(x−3)+2. Identify its vertex.
Independent Try It 4 — Reciprocal combined shift. Transform y=1/x one unit right and one up.
Independent Try It 5 — Reflect an absolute value graph. Reflect f(x)=|x−1| about x-axis and about y-axis separately.
Independent Try It 6 — Reflect finite table. If f(−1)=5,f(0)=8,f(2)=3, create tables for −f(x) and f(−x).
Independent Try It 7 — Reflect an even function. Given f(x)=x², find −f(x) and f(−x). Explain difference.
Independent Try It 8 — Even or odd polynomial. Classify f(x)=x⁴+2x²+5.
Independent Try It 9 — Compress vertical table. Given f(1)=8, f(2)=12, f(3)=16, find g(x)=(3/4)f(x).
Independent Try It 10 — Stretch and translate identity. Vertically stretch f(x)=x by 3 and then shift down 2.
Independent Try It 11 — Stretch square root horizontally. Construct √x stretched horizontally by 3.

KeyConcepts.Title: Vertical shifts
KeyConcepts.Definition: g(x)=f(x)+k moves a graph vertically by k output units.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Domain unchanged; range shifts by k.

KeyConcepts.Title: Horizontal shifts
KeyConcepts.Definition: g(x)=f(x−h) shifts right h; f(x+h) shifts left h.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Input changes have opposite sign to visual displacement.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reflections
KeyConcepts.Definition: −f(x) reflects across x-axis; f(−x) reflects across y-axis.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Negating output differs from negating input.
KeyConcepts.Example: −√x has nonpositive range, √(−x) has nonpositive domain.

KeyConcepts.Title: Even/odd parity
KeyConcepts.Definition: Even means f(−x)=f(x); odd means f(−x)=−f(x).
KeyConcepts.Rule: Verify domain symmetry and algebra; many functions are neither.
KeyConcepts.Example: x² is even, x³ is odd, (x−1)² neither.

KeyConcepts.Title: Vertical scale
KeyConcepts.Definition: g(x)=a·f(x) stretches for |a|>1 and compresses for 0<|a|<1.

KeyConcepts.Title: Horizontal scale
KeyConcepts.Definition: g(x)=f(bx) compresses horizontally if |b|>1 and stretches if 0<|b|<1.
KeyConcepts.Example: f(3x) shifts old features x=6 to x=2.

KeyConcepts.Title: Combined transformations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Apply inside input changes, then output changes; factor inner affine term to locate horizontal shift.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Transform endpoints and preserve allowed-domain preimages.
KeyConcepts.Example: f((x+2)/2)−3 shifts stretched graph left 2 and down 3.

SummaryPoints: Output shifts f(x)+k move the graph vertically by k.
Input shifts f(x−h) move graph horizontally right h.
−f(x) reflects outputs; f(−x) reflects input coordinates.
Even functions satisfy f(−x)=f(x), odd functions satisfy f(−x)=−f(x).
Outside multiplication scales vertically; inside multiplication scales inversely horizontally.
Preserve valid original domain restrictions under every transformation.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Moving a graph left for f(x−3).
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Input−3 is matched at x three units larger.
Horizontal and vertical reflections affect different coordinates.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use f(−x) for y-axis reflection, −f(x) for x-axis reflection.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating f(3x) as a threefold horizontal stretch.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The input attains prior values at one-third its previous x.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Classifying a function as even/odd without symmetric domain.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: f(−x) must be defined whenever f(x) is.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Verify both domain symmetry and parity identity.
